previous_statement: The preceding two steps, the triangle inequality, and node 1.1 imply ||h_n(Z)||^2 <= ||h_n(Z^dagger dot Z)||+C_prod*e||Z||^2 <= ((1+kappa*e)b_n+C_prod*e)||Z||^2. Taking the supremum over ||Z||=1 yields b_n^2 <= (1+kappa*e)b_n+C_prod*e.
new_statement: From nodes 1.2.3.1 and 1.2.2 one obtains, for every n and Z, ||h_n(Z)||^2 <= b_n||Z^dagger dot Z||+C_prod*e||Z||^2. At n=1, node 1.1 supplies ||Z^dagger dot Z|| <= (1+kappa_1*e)||Z||^2, hence b_1^2 <= (1+kappa_1*e)b_1+C_prod*e (with the zero-corner case giving b_1=0). For n>1, node 1.1 explicitly records that the allowed inputs supply no universal amplified estimate ||Z^dagger dot Z|| <= (1+kappa*e)||Z||^2. Therefore the displayed all-n quadratic inequality does not follow in the permitted dependency scope; an additional uniform amplified-corner norm theorem is required.
